# Getting Started

One of the principles behind IGDB.com is accessibility of data. We wish to share the data with anyone who wants to build cool video game oriented websites, apps and services.

This means that you are not only contributing to the value of IGDB but to thousands of other projects as well. We are looking forward to see what exciting game related projects you come up with. Happy coding!

For a high level overview of our juicy data, check out the [endpoints section](#endpoints).

## Account Creation

In order to use our API, you must have a Twitch Account.

1.  Sign Up with [Twitch](https://dev.twitch.tv/login) for a free account
2.  Ensure you have Two Factor Authentication [enabled](https://www.twitch.tv/settings/security)
3.  Register your application in the [Twitch Developer Portal](https://dev.twitch.tv/console/apps/create)
    *   The OAuth Redirect URL field is not used by IGDB. Please add ’localhost’ to continue.
    *   The Client Type must be set to `Confidential` to generate Client Secrets
4.  [Manage](https://dev.twitch.tv/console/apps) your newly created application
5.  Generate a Client Secret by pressing \[New Secret\]
6.  Take note of the Client ID and Client Secret

The IGDB.com API is free for **non-commercial** usage under the terms of the [Twitch Developer Service Agreement](https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/developer-agreement/).

## Authentication

Now that you have a Client ID and Client Secret you will be authenticating as a Twitch Developer using Oauth2.  
 Detailed information can be found in the [Twitch Developer Docs](https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/authentication).

Make a `POST` request to `https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/token` with the following query string parameters, substituting your Client ID and Client Secret accordingly.

`client_id=Client ID`

`client_secret=Client Secret`

`grant_type=client_credentials`

### Example

If your Client ID is `abcdefg12345` and your Client Secret is `hijklmn67890`, the whole url should look like the following.

```yaml
POST: https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/token?client_id=abcdefg12345&client_secret=hijklmn67890&grant_type=client_credentials
```

The response from this will be a json object containing the access token and the number of second until the token expires.

```json
{
  "access_token": "access12345token",
  "expires_in": 5587808,
  "token_type": "bearer"
}
```

## Requests

*   Most of the requests to the API will use the `POST` method
*   The base URL is: **[https://api.igdb.com/v4](https://api.igdb.com/v4)**
*   You define which endpoint you wish to query by appending `/{endpoint name}` to the base URL eg. **[https://api.igdb.com/v4/games](https://api.igdb.com/v4/games)**
*   Include your `Client ID` and `Access Token` in the `HEADER` of your request so that your headers look like the following.
    *   Take special care of the capitalisation. `Bearer` should be hard-coded infront of your `access_token`

```yaml
Client-ID: Client ID
Authorization: Bearer access_token
```

*   You use the `BODY` of your request to specify the fields you want to retrieve as well as any other filters, sorting etc

### Example

If your Client ID is `abcdefg12345` and your access\_token is `access12345token`, a simple request to get information about 10 games would be.

```yaml
POST: https://api.igdb.com/v4/games
Client-ID: abcdefg12345
Authorization: Bearer access12345token
Body: "fields *;"
```

### More Examples

You can find some examples requests [here](#examples)

## Rate Limits

There is a rate limit of **4 requests per second**. If you go over this limit you will receive a response with status code `429 Too Many Requests`.

You are able to have up to 8 _open_ requests at any moment in time. This can occur if requests take longer than 1 second to respond when multiple requests are being made.

## Wrappers

Get setup quickly by using one of these wrappers!

### Apicalypse

*   [NodeJS](https://github.com/igdb/node-apicalypse)
*   [JVM/Kotlin/Java](https://github.com/husnjak/IGDB-API-JVM)
*   [Swift](https://github.com/husnjak/IGDB-SWIFT-API)
*   [Python](https://github.com/twitchtv/igdb-api-python)

### Third Party

*   [PHP/Laravel](https://github.com/marcreichel/igdb-laravel)
*   [GO](https://github.com/Henry-Sarabia/apicalypse)
*   [Ruby](https://github.com/ad2games/ruby-apicalypse)
*   [C#/.NET](https://github.com/kamranayub/igdb-dotnet)
*   [Deno](https://github.com/killoblanco/igdb-api-deno)

### Third Party Documentation

*   [OpenAPI Documentation](https://igdb-openapi.s-crypt.co/)
*   [Postman Collection](https://www.postman.com/aceprosports/workspace/public/collection/18853756-4367eb1d-3f6b-41ee-96cb-3ccb3d094a5c)

# Examples

It’s recommended to try out your queries in an API viewer like [Postman](https://www.postman.com/) or [Insomnia](https://insomnia.rest/) before using code. This helps you find problems a lot sooner!

Postman setup example

![](images/postman1.png)

![](images/postman2.png)

### A very basic example to retrieve the name for 10 games.

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/)**

```
fields name; limit 10;
```

### Get all information from a specific game

1942, is the ID of a game.

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/)**

```
fields *; where id = 1942;
```

### Exclude irrelevant data from your query

Remove alternative\_name from your result query

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/platforms/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/platforms/)**

```
fields *;
exclude alternative_name;
```

### Get all games from specific genres

Notice how you can comma separate multiple IDs (8, 9, and 11). You can do this with games, companies and anything else. Also note that when you have multiple IDs they have to be surrounded by a parenthesis. Single ids can be queried both with and without the parenthesis.

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/genres/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/genres/)**

```
fields *; where id = (8,9,11);
```

### Count total games that have a rating higher than 75

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/count](https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/count)**

```
where rating > 75;
```

### Order by rating

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/)**

```
fields name,rating; sort rating desc;
```

### Coming soon games for Playstation 4

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/release\_dates/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/release_dates/)**

```
fields *; where game.platforms = 48 & date > 1538129354; sort date asc;
```

1538129354: Is the timestamp in milliseconds of 28/09/2018 (This you need to generate yourself) 48 Is the platform id of Playstation 4.

### Recently released games for Playstation 4

```
fields *; where game.platforms = 48 & date < 1538129354; sort date desc;
```

### Search, return certain fields.

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/)**

```
search "Halo"; fields name,release_dates.human;
```

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/)**

```
fields name, involved_companies; search "Halo";
```

### Search games but exclude versions (editions)

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/)**

```
fields name, involved_companies; search "Assassins Creed"; where version_parent = null;
```

This will return search results with ID and name of the game but exclude editions such as “Collectors Edition”.

### Searching all endpoints

The example below searches for “Sonic the Hedgehog” which will find the Character Sonic, the collection Soninc the Hedgehog. And of course also several games with names containing Sonic the Hedgehog.

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/search](https://api.igdb.com/v4/search)**

```
fields *; search "sonic the hedgehog"; limit 50;
```

### Get versions (editions) of a game

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/game\_versions/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/game_versions/)**

```
fields game.name,games.name; where game = 28540;
```

The resulting object will contain all games that are a version of the game with id 28540

### Get the parent game for a version

**[https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/](https://api.igdb.com/v4/games/)**

```
fields version_parent.*; where id = 39047;
```

The resulting object will contain all main games

### Get all games that are playstation 4 exclusives

```
fields name,category,platforms;
where category = 0 & platforms = 48;
```

### Get all games that are only released on playstation 4 AND PC

```
fields name,category,platforms;
where category = 0 & platforms = {48,6};
```

Contents of https://openverse.org/about:
# About Openverse

Openverse is a tool that allows openly licensed and public domain works to be discovered and used by everyone.

Openverse searches across more than 800 million images and audio tracks from open APIs and the [Common Crawl](https://commoncrawl.org/) dataset. We aggregate works from multiple public repositories, and facilitate reuse through features like one-click attribution.

Currently Openverse only searches images and audio tracks, with search for video provided through External Sources. We plan to add additional media types such as open texts and 3D models, with the ultimate goal of providing access to the estimated 2.5 billion CC licensed and public domain works on the web. All of our code is open source and can be accessed at the [Openverse GitHub repository](https://github.com/wordpress/openverse). We [welcome community contribution](https://make.wordpress.org/openverse/). You can see what [we’re currently working on](https://github.com/orgs/WordPress/projects/3).

Openverse is the successor to CC Search which was launched by Creative Commons in 2019, after its migration to WordPress in 2021. You can read more about this transition in the official announcements from [Creative Commons](https://creativecommons.org/2021/05/03/cc-search-to-join-wordpress/) and [WordPress](https://ma.tt/2021/04/cc-search-to-join-wordpress-org/). We remain committed to our goal of tackling discoverability and accessibility of open access media.

Openverse does not verify licensing information for individual works, or whether the generated attribution is accurate or complete. Please independently verify the licensing status and attribution information before reusing the content. For more details, read the [Openverse Terms of Use](https://creativecommons.org/terms/).

## External Sources

Openverse is built on top of a catalog that indexes CC-licensed and public domain content from selected sources. Learn more about our [sources here](/sources).

However, there are many sources of CC-licensed and public domain media that we are not yet able to include in Openverse search. This might be because they do not offer a public API, or that our contributors have not yet had time to integrate them into Openverse. These are valued sources and we want to make sure that you are able to find the best openly licensed materials possible, regardless of where they are located.

You can find links to external sources at the bottom of every Openverse search results page; on pages for searches which return no results; and on pages for media types we do not yet support but intend to.

This functionality also allows us to start conversations and build relationships with sources that may like to be included in Openverse in the future. Finally, we can also offer external sources of media types we do not include in Openverse yet, but plan to.

## Can I suggest new external sources?

Yes, please! Create an [issue](https://github.com/WordPress/openverse/issues) in our GitHub repository or send us an [email](mailto:openverse@wordpress.org) and tell us about the new sources you’d like to see included.

## Why did you build this?

For many years, Creative Commons has offered its users a dedicated search portal for searching platforms that have CC licensing filters built in. In fact, this is still maintained at [oldsearch.creativecommons.org](https://oldsearch.creativecommons.org).

For users of the legacy CC Meta Search site, the "External Sources" feature on Openverse will look familiar. The goal was to ensure that the functionality is not lost, but is updated and embedded within our new search engine for openly licensed content. Additionally, the "External Sources" feature builds on this functionality, allowing us to quickly add new external sources as we discover them, and support new content types in the future.

We hope you enjoy, and if you have suggestions for improvement, leave us [feedback](/feedback).

 # Database Design
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - MySQL 8, InnoDB, `utf8mb4`, and UTC timestamps.
 - Use `BIGINT UNSIGNED` identifiers (or consistently adopted UUIDs) and foreign keys for relational integrity.
 - Store money as `BIGINT` integer minor units with an ISO 4217 currency code. Never use floating-point columns for prices.
 - Use `created_at` and `updated_at` where records change; use explicit statuses instead of deleting records whose history matters.
 - Store password hashes from `password_hash()` only. Never store plaintext passwords, session tokens, or plaintext digital keys.
 
 ## Tables
 
 The following is a logical schema; migrations should define exact lengths, nullability, constraints, and indexes.
 
 ### Identity
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `users` | `id`, `email` (unique), `password_hash`, `display_name`, `role`, `status`, timestamps | `role` is `customer` or a tightly controlled `admin`; `status` can disable access. |
 | `sessions` | `id`, `user_id`, `token_hash` (unique), `csrf_token_hash`, `expires_at`, `created_at`, `last_seen_at`, `revoked_at` | Store only a hash of the random cookie token. Session rows permit revocation and expiry. |
 | `seller_profiles` | `id`, `user_id` (unique), `display_name`, `status`, timestamps | A seller is a user with a seller profile; approval/status is server controlled. |
 
 ### Catalog and offers
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `products` | `id`, `slug` (unique), `name`, `description`, `image_url`, `status`, timestamps | Represents a catalog item; offers carry sale-specific platform and region details. |
 | `categories` | `id`, `slug` (unique), `name`, `status`, `sort_order` | A product may belong to multiple categories. |
 | `product_categories` | `product_id`, `category_id` | Composite primary key; many-to-many join. |
 | `platforms` | `id`, `code` (unique), `name`, `status` | Examples: PC, PlayStation, Xbox. |
 | `regions` | `id`, `code` (unique), `name`, `status` | Examples: global, EU, US. |
 | `offers` | `id`, `product_id`, `seller_id`, `platform_id`, `region_id`, `price_minor`, `compare_at_price_minor` (nullable), `currency`, `status`, `deal_starts_at`, `deal_ends_at`, timestamps | `seller_id` references `seller_profiles`; an offer identifies what is being sold and by whom. `price_minor` is the current selling price. `compare_at_price_minor` is the reference price used to calculate and display a discount; it is null when no comparison price is advertised. |
 | `digital_keys` | `id`, `offer_id`, `ciphertext`, `nonce`, `key_version`, `status`, `order_item_id` (nullable foreign key), timestamps | `status`: `available`, `sold`, or `disabled`. Ciphertext is authenticated-encrypted; each key row can be assigned to at most one order item. Never expose this table directly. |
 
 ### Shopping and order history
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `carts` | `id`, `user_id` (unique), timestamps | One active cart per user in the MVP. |
 | `cart_items` | `id`, `cart_id`, `offer_id`, `quantity`, timestamps | Unique `(cart_id, offer_id)`; quantity is positive and bounded by available keys at checkout. |
 | `orders` | `id`, `user_id`, `status`, `currency`, `subtotal_minor`, `total_minor`, `idempotency_key`, `created_at`, `paid_at` | Unique `(user_id, idempotency_key)` when an idempotency key is supplied. Simulated payment status is recorded here. |
 | `order_items` | `id`, `order_id`, `offer_id`, `product_name_snapshot`, `seller_name_snapshot`, `platform_name_snapshot`, `region_name_snapshot`, `quantity`, `unit_price_minor`, `currency` | Immutable purchase-time snapshots; offer may later change or be disabled. |
 | `key_access_logs` | `id`, `user_id`, `order_item_id`, `accessed_at`, `request_id` | Audit metadata only. Never store the returned plaintext key in logs. |
 
 ### Homepage content
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `hero_banners` | `id`, `title`, `image_url`, `target_url`, `sort_order`, `starts_at`, `ends_at`, `status` | Only active, in-window banners are returned. |
 
 Best sellers, special deals, and popular categories are computed from order/offer data in the MVP rather than duplicated into mutable homepage tables. If editorial curation or query load later warrants it, add a materialized/cache table with an explicit refresh strategy.
 
 An offer qualifies as a special deal only when it is active, within its configured deal window, has available key inventory, and has a non-null `compare_at_price_minor` greater than `price_minor`. Calculate the discount from the two integer amounts in the same currency; do not persist a separate percentage that can become stale. Treat a null comparison price (or one not greater than the selling price) as no advertised discount.
 
 ### Search support
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `product_search_grams` | `product_id`, `gram`, `weight` | Derived two/three-character gram index for typo-tolerant fallback; unique `(product_id, gram)`, index `(gram, product_id)`. Rebuild when product names or active status change. |
 
 MySQL `FULLTEXT` over product name and description provides first-pass relevance and token-prefix search. Gram rows are derived data generated from normalized active product names. The repeatable seed refreshes them, and `php backend/bin/rebuild-search-index.php` rebuilds them after catalog name/status changes. Search normalization uses PHP `intl` and `mbstring`; these extensions must be enabled in the backend runtime. See `API.md` for query bounds, fallback behavior, and response metadata.
 
 ## Relationships
 
 - `users` 1—0..1 `seller_profiles`: customers may also have an approved seller profile.
 - `users` 1—many `sessions`: one user can have multiple devices/sessions; revocation is per session.
 - `products` many—many `categories` through `product_categories`.
 - `products`, `seller_profiles`, `platforms`, and `regions` each have a one—many relationship to `offers`.
 - `offers` 1—many `digital_keys`: each key is stock for one specific offer.
 - `users` 1—1 active `carts`; `carts` 1—many `cart_items`; each cart item references one offer.
 - `users` 1—many `orders`; `orders` 1—many `order_items`; each item references its original offer and stores purchase snapshots.
 - `order_items` 1—many `digital_keys` after purchase (one per purchased unit); each key row's nullable `order_item_id` foreign key can refer to only one order item, while allowing multiple keys for an item with quantity greater than one.
 - `users` and `order_items` 1—many `key_access_logs` rows provide an access audit trail.
 - `products` 1—many derived `product_search_grams` rows.
 
 ## Constraints and indexes
 
 Add indexes for:
 
 - Unique `users.email`, `products.slug`, category/platform/region codes, `sessions.token_hash`, and seller profile `user_id`.
 - `offers(product_id, status)`, `offers(platform_id, region_id, status, price_minor)`, and `offers(seller_id, status)`.
 - `digital_keys(offer_id, status, id)` for availability/locking and `digital_keys(order_item_id)` for order delivery.
 - `cart_items(cart_id, offer_id)` unique; `orders(user_id, created_at)`; `order_items(order_id)`.
 - `product_categories(category_id, product_id)` and gram lookup `(gram, product_id)`.
 - A MySQL full-text index on active-search fields where supported by the chosen query design.
 
 Use foreign-key deletion rules deliberately: restrict deletes for products/offers referenced in order history; soft-disable catalog and seller records instead. Cascading deletion is appropriate only for disposable derived data such as search grams.
 
 ## Key inventory and checkout consistency
 
 Available inventory is the count of `digital_keys` with `status='available'`, not a client-provided stock value. During checkout, lock the required available key rows (for example with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) in a transaction. Assign keys and create order records atomically. A unique assignment plus transaction rollback prevents double sale. Use a consistent lock order and bounded retries for deadlock errors.
 
 The simulated payment operation must not report success until the order and all requested keys have been committed as sold. If a future real payment provider is introduced, do not hold a database transaction open during a network call: add a reservation/expiry and payment-confirmation workflow, then fulfill idempotently after verified provider confirmation.

 - Money uses `{ "amountMinor": 1299, "currency": "EUR" }`.
 - Paginated lists use `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "page": 1, "perPage": 24, "total": 42 } }`. Bounded section and lookup lists use `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "limit": 8 } }`.
 - Errors use `{ "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "...", "fields": {} , "requestId": "..." } }`. Omit `fields` when inapplicable. Never return SQL, stack traces, secrets, or key ciphertext.
 - Use `400` for malformed input, `401` for missing/invalid authentication, `403` for insufficient permission/CSRF failure, `404` for missing resources, `409` for conflicts/insufficient inventory, `422` for semantic validation failures, and `429` for throttling.
 - Apply bounded pagination and allowlisted sort fields/directions. Never interpolate unchecked request values into SQL.
 - State-changing requests require CSRF validation. Do not enable permissive CORS.
 
 ## Implemented scope through Phase 3
 
 Phases 2B and 3 implement the health check, product catalog and reference-data lookups, four independent homepage endpoints, product search, and product detail with seller-offer comparison. Authentication, registration, login/logout, cart, checkout, orders, and digital-key delivery remain future-phase contracts.
 
 An empty result is a successful response (`200`) with `"data": []`. The API does not invent sales or inventory to populate a section. In particular, best sellers require completed orders in the recent period, and special deals require available digital-key inventory. The current demo seed intentionally creates neither.

 ## Catalog, search, product
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/products` | Product catalog with bounded filters, sorting, and pagination. |
 | `GET` | `/categories` | Active category filter options. |
 | `GET` | `/platforms` | Active platform filter options. |
 | `GET` | `/regions` | Active region filter options. |
 | `GET` | `/search` | Global search with typo and partial-word tolerance. |
 | `GET` | `/products/{slug}` | Active product details and approved sellers' active offers for comparison. |
 
 `GET /products` query parameters:
 
 - `page` (default `1`, positive integer)
 - `perPage` (default `20`, integer `1..48`)
 - `platform`, `region`, and `category` (active code/slug values)
 - `currency` (three-letter code, default `EUR`)
 - `minPriceMinor`, `maxPriceMinor` (non-negative integer minor units in the selected currency)
 - `sort`: `newest` (default), `price_asc`, `price_desc`, or `popular`
 
 The catalog lists active products. `lowestOffer` is the least expensive matching active offer in the selected currency and optional platform/region filters; it is `null` when the product has no matching active offer. An offer with no available keys is still represented with `availableQuantity: 0`. Price filters apply to the selected offer after currency/platform/region filters. Products are ordered deterministically within each sort. `popular` uses paid units from the last 30 days and breaks ties by newest product.
 
 Paginated response:
 
 ```json
 {
   "data": [
     {
       "id": 1,
       "slug": "starlight-odyssey",
       "name": "Starlight Odyssey",
       "description": "A fictional role-playing adventure.",
       "imageUrl": null,
       "lowestOffer": {
         "offerId": 1,
         "priceMinor": 1899,
         "compareAtPriceMinor": 4999,
         "currency": "EUR",
         "platform": { "code": "pc", "name": "PC" },
         "region": { "code": "global", "name": "Global" },
         "availableQuantity": 0,
         "discountPercent": 62
       }
     }
   ],
   "meta": { "page": 1, "perPage": 20, "total": 3, "sort": "newest", "currency": "EUR" }
 }
 ```
 
 Invalid, unsupported, or out-of-range query values return `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` with a `fields` map. An empty page returns `200`, an empty `data` array, and pagination metadata.
 
 Lookup endpoints accept no query parameters and return active options. Categories are ordered by `sort_order` then name; platforms and regions are ordered by name:
 
 ```json
 { "data": [{ "id": 1, "slug": "action", "name": "Action" }], "meta": { "limit": 100 } }
 { "data": [{ "id": 1, "code": "pc", "name": "PC" }], "meta": { "limit": 100 } }
 { "data": [{ "id": 1, "code": "global", "name": "Global" }], "meta": { "limit": 100 } }
 ```
 
 The three examples correspond to `/categories`, `/platforms`, and `/regions`, respectively.
 
 `compareAtPriceMinor` is null when the offer has no advertised comparison price. The API calculates any displayed discount from the compare-at and current prices, in the offer's currency; it must not trust a client-supplied percentage. An offer is eligible for the special-deals section only when the compare-at price is greater than the current price and the offer is active, in its deal window, and has available inventory.
 
 `GET /search` accepts:
 
 - `q` (required; 2–100 normalized letters/numbers; raw input up to 200 characters)
 - `page` (default `1`, positive integer up to `10000`)
 - `perPage` (default `20`, integer `1..48`)
 - The same `platform`, `region`, `category`, `currency`, `minPriceMinor`, and `maxPriceMinor` filters as `/products`
 - `sort`: `relevance` (default), `newest`, `price_asc`, `price_desc`, or `popular`
 
 Queries are Unicode NFKC-normalized, case-folded, and reduced to letter/number tokens with collapsed whitespace. MySQL FULLTEXT natural-language and token-prefix matches are ranked first. When fewer than eight FULLTEXT candidates are found, the API merges up to 1,000 candidates from the derived product-name gram index. It applies the product's catalog filters before scoring title similarity in PHP, which is limited to 100 products; ordinary catalog requests do not invoke fuzzy scoring.
 
 Search response:
 
 ```json
 {
   "data": [
     {
       "id": 1,
       "slug": "starlight-odyssey",
       "name": "Starlight Odyssey",
       "description": "A fictional role-playing adventure.",
       "imageUrl": "/images/starlight-odyssey.svg",
       "lowestOffer": {
         "offerId": 1,
         "priceMinor": 1899,
         "compareAtPriceMinor": 4999,
         "currency": "EUR",
         "platform": { "code": "pc", "name": "PC" },
         "region": { "code": "global", "name": "Global" },
         "availableQuantity": 0,
         "discountPercent": 62
       }
     }
   ],
   "meta": {
     "q": "starlight ody",
     "page": 1,
     "perPage": 20,
     "total": 1,
     "sort": "relevance",
     "currency": "EUR",
     "candidateLimit": 100,
     "capped": false
   }
 }
 ```
 
 `meta.total` describes the filtered, ranked results in the bounded scored set. `capped` is true when 100 eligible scoring candidates (or the 1,000-result lexical pool) are reached; in that case, more matches may exist beyond this page set. Invalid or too-short queries return `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`; an unmatched query returns `200` with empty `data`. Search-specific request rate limiting is deferred to Phase 6; query length, pagination, and candidate count are bounded in this phase.
 
 `GET /products/{slug}` returns `404 NOT_FOUND` when the product is missing or inactive. Only active products and active offers from approved sellers with active platform/region options are exposed. Offers include zero-stock rows so availability is explicit and are grouped by currency, then ordered by price and offer ID within each currency; amounts in different currencies are not treated as directly comparable. A product with no qualifying offers returns an empty `offers` list.

 The browser can select an offer for display, but does not reserve inventory or create a cart in Phase 3.
 
 This hybrid is practical without another service at early scale. If catalog size, language requirements, or search latency outgrow it, migrate search behind the same endpoint to a dedicated engine such as Meilisearch or OpenSearch.
 
 ## Cart and checkout
 
 Reserved for Phase 4; not implemented through Phase 3.
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/cart` | Return current user's cart with current offer data, stock, and recalculated totals. |
 | `POST` | `/cart/items` | Add an offer and quantity; body `{ "offerId": 123, "quantity": 1 }`. |
 | `PATCH` | `/cart/items/{id}` | Change quantity; validate positive bounded quantity. |
 | `DELETE` | `/cart/items/{id}` | Remove an item. |
 | `POST` | `/checkout` | Authenticated simulated checkout. Accept an idempotency key; server revalidates prices/currency and locks inventory. |
 
 Checkout response on success: `201` with order ID, status, currency, totals, and purchase item summaries. It must not include plaintext keys in the initial response; users retrieve delivery through the order endpoint after the order is committed as paid.
 
 ## Orders and key delivery
 
 Reserved for Phase 5; not implemented through Phase 3.
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/orders` | Current user's paginated order history. |
 | `GET` | `/orders/{id}` | Current user's order and item summaries; enforce ownership. |
 | `GET` | `/orders/{id}/keys` | Return plaintext purchased keys only after verifying ownership and paid status. Record an access audit event; do not cache the response. |
 
 Set key-response cache headers to `Cache-Control: no-store`; do not include keys in URLs, analytics, client logs, or error reporting. Consider allowing repeat reveal by the owning user for MVP support, with each retrieval audited. One-time retrieval adds account-recovery and delivery-failure complexity and is not assumed here.
 
 ## Admin and seller operations
 
 Admin catalog, banner, seller moderation, offer management, and key upload endpoints are deliberately not part of the customer MVP contract. If required for a usable seeded demo, add narrowly authorized admin routes in a separate phase. Never expose bulk key data in ordinary seller/catalog endpoints.

 # Implementation Plan
 
 ## Guiding sequence
 
 Build a thin vertical slice early, then extend it with tested business flows. Keep the approved React/PHP/MySQL stack; do not introduce a payment or search service before requirements justify it.
 
 ## Phase 0 — Confirm boundaries
 
 - Review and approve the architecture and assumptions in these documents.
 - Confirm MVP deployment origin, currencies, seller/admin scope, and how demo users and inventory will be seeded.
 - Keep checkout explicitly simulated. Decide separately before adding any real payment integration.
 
 **Exit:** agreed scope and architecture; no app stack initialized before approval.
 
 ## Phase 1 — Project foundation and data model
 
 - Initialize React/TypeScript/Vite/Tailwind/React Router and the PHP API only after approval.
 - Add environment configuration examples, PHP front controller, API response/error conventions, and same-origin local proxy configuration.
 - Add MySQL migrations for identity, catalog, offers, cart, orders, encrypted key inventory, and banners; seed reproducible demo data.
 - Add smoke tests for API startup, DB connection, migrations, and health/status endpoint.
 
 **Exit:** repeatable local setup and migrations; no secrets committed.
 
 ## Phase 2 — Design system, catalog, and homepage
 
 ### 2A — Establish the design system
 
 - Add semantic CSS custom properties and Tailwind mappings for the approved palette: background `#4518AC`, sections `#311178`, cards/footer `#1F0A4D`, text `#FFFFFF`, savings `#83E916`, and region labels `#E66A8C`.
 - Apply square geometry globally: zero border radius for page sections, cards, controls, badges, banners, and footer elements.
 - Define shared type, spacing, border, surface, and focus styles alongside the supplied palette so pages do not invent isolated visual values.
 - Establish responsive grid breakpoints with two columns on mobile, three on tablet, and five on desktop.
 - Implement reusable layout and UI components: prominent navigation/search, rectangular promo banner, section container, product card/grid, price and discount display, region label, catalog controls, seller offer row, footer, and loading/empty/error states.
 - Design blueprints for the remaining store flows (search, product detail, authentication, cart, checkout, confirmation, and order history) so they can use the same tokens and shell in their later implementation phases.
 - Check text and focus contrast on each surface; use lime and pink as indicators on dark purple surfaces where needed for readability.
 
 **Exit:** the token layer and shared components implement the supplied visual direction; the reusable product grid is verified at representative mobile, tablet, and desktop viewport widths.
 
 ### 2B — Catalog and homepage
 
 - Implement PDO repositories/services for products, categories, platforms, regions, hero banners, sales summaries, and eligible special deals.
 - Implement `GET /products`, `GET /categories`, `GET /platforms`, `GET /regions`, and the four independent homepage endpoints. Document every implemented endpoint and response format in `docs/API.md`.
 - Connect catalog filter, sort, price range, and pagination controls to the API; keep each homepage section's loading, error, retry, and empty states independent.
 - Build the responsive homepage and catalog using the shared components: large rectangular promotional banners, clearly separated sections, and dense dark product cards with artwork, prices, discounts, and region labels.
 - Seed fictional products, a disabled demo seller, price-bearing offers without digital keys, and an original banner asset. Do not seed completed orders or pretend inventory exists; best sellers, popular categories, and in-stock special deals stay empty until their qualifying data exists.
 - Keep authentication, checkout, orders, and digital-key delivery out of this phase.
 - Add request validation and focused API tests for filters, paging, empty states, and inactive records.
 
 **Exit:** homepage sections are served independently from the backend; catalog filters are server-enforced; homepage and catalog use the approved design system and responsive 5/3/2-column grids.
 
 ## Phase 3 — Search and product comparison
 
 - Implement `GET /search` using Unicode-normalized input, MySQL FULLTEXT natural/prefix matching, a bounded gram-index fallback, and relevance-first pagination. Apply catalog filters before scoring no more than 100 candidates.
 - Maintain the derived name-gram index during seeding and provide an explicit rebuild command for catalog name/status changes. Cap fuzzy candidates at 100; defer search request rate limiting to Phase 6.
 - Implement `GET /products/{slug}` with active product details and active offers from approved sellers, including seller, platform, region, compare-at/current price, discount, and available inventory.
 - Add distinct fictional sellers and comparable offers for demo product detail pages without adding digital keys or implying stock.
 - Connect the global search bar to a URL-backed results page with loading, error, empty, retry, filter, and pagination states. Make product cards link to detail pages.
 - Build a seller comparison view where price, seller, platform, region, and stock status are visible together; allow a customer to select an offer for display without implementing cart/checkout behavior.
 - Document API request/response contracts and the search index lifecycle. Test exact, partial, typo, no-result, validation, filters, pagination, candidate bounds, product not-found, seller ordering, and inactive records.
 
 **Exit:** exact, partial, and typo-tolerant queries return relevant active products within the candidate bound; product details clearly compare active seller offers and their region and availability without implying inventory that is not present.
 
 ## Phase 4 — Authentication and cart
 
 - Implement hashed passwords, opaque server-side sessions, CSRF protection, session rotation/revocation, and rate limits on authentication.
 - Add registration/login/logout/me flows, protected route UX, and authenticated cart endpoints.
 - Recalculate cart prices and totals from current server-side offers on every read/checkout.
 - Test unauthenticated access, CSRF failures, session expiry/logout, and cart quantity validation.
 
 **Exit:** private data is bound to the authenticated user; frontend route guards complement but do not replace API authorization.
 
 ## Phase 5 — Simulated checkout and secure delivery
 
 - Implement transactional, idempotent checkout with locked available keys, purchase snapshots, and consistent order state.
 - Implement order history/details and owner-checked key retrieval after successful simulated payment only.
 - Encrypt keys at ingestion, restrict decryption to delivery service, disable key-response caching, and add audit logging.
 - Test concurrent attempts against low inventory, retries with the same idempotency key, rollback paths, and unauthorized key access.
 
 **Exit:** no key can be assigned twice or disclosed before a committed paid order.
 
 ## Phase 6 — Hardening and release readiness
 
 - Review all endpoints for authorization, validation, SQL parameterization, CSRF, output encoding, and rate limiting.
 - Verify responsive accessibility, loading/empty/error states, and complete order journey.
 - Add structured server logging without secrets, production error handling, backup/restore notes, and operational configuration.
 - Run targeted suites, then the full test/build/type-check/lint commands that exist in the initialized project.
 
 **Exit:** reproducible deployment configuration, documented limitations, and verified customer workflows.
 
 ## Priority order
 
 1. Schema, catalog, inventory model, and API error/auth conventions.
 2. Independently fetched homepage sections and usable product catalog.
 3. Product comparison and typo-tolerant search.
 4. Authentication/session/CSRF and protected account state.
 5. Cart and simulated transactional checkout.
 6. Encrypted digital-key delivery and order history.
 7. Admin tooling, seller lifecycle, real payments, refunds, tax, and advanced merchandising only after scope approval.
 
 ## Risk-driven acceptance checks
 
 - All prices and inventory are recomputed server-side.
 - Checkout is atomic and safe to retry; insufficient inventory is an explicit conflict.
 - An order cannot be read or delivered by another user.
 - Key endpoints do not reveal content before paid status and do not cache it.
 - Home sections load independently; a failure in one does not hide the others.
 - Search fuzzy matching is bounded, measurable, and does not degrade ordinary catalog browsing.
 - Search request throttling is implemented during Phase 6 hardening; Phase 3 bounds query size, page size, and fuzzy candidates.
 - The specified palette and zero-radius geometry are applied consistently through reusable components.
 - Homepage and catalog grids render two columns on mobile, three on tablet, and five on desktop.

 # REST API
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - Base path: `/api/v1`; all endpoints return JSON.
 - Browser calls use same-origin HTTPS. Authenticated endpoints (implemented in a later phase) use an `HttpOnly` session cookie.
 - Money uses `{ "amountMinor": 1299, "currency": "EUR" }`.
 - Paginated lists use `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "page": 1, "perPage": 24, "total": 42 } }`. Bounded section and lookup lists use `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "limit": 8 } }`.
 - Errors use `{ "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "...", "fields": {} , "requestId": "..." } }`. Omit `fields` when inapplicable. Never return SQL, stack traces, secrets, or key ciphertext.
 - Use `400` for malformed input, `401` for missing/invalid authentication, `403` for insufficient permission/CSRF failure, `404` for missing resources, `409` for conflicts/insufficient inventory, `422` for semantic validation failures, and `429` for throttling.
 - Apply bounded pagination and allowlisted sort fields/directions. Never interpolate unchecked request values into SQL.
 - State-changing requests require CSRF validation. Do not enable permissive CORS.
 
 ## Implemented scope through Phase 3
 
 Phases 2B and 3 implement the health check, product catalog and reference-data lookups, four independent homepage endpoints, product search, and product detail with seller-offer comparison. Authentication, registration, login/logout, cart, checkout, orders, and digital-key delivery remain future-phase contracts.
 
 An empty result is a successful response (`200`) with `"data": []`. The API does not invent sales or inventory to populate a section. In particular, best sellers require completed orders in the recent period, and special deals require available digital-key inventory. The current demo seed intentionally creates neither.
 
 ## Health
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/health` | Verify API and database connectivity. |
 
 Successful response (`200`):
 
 ```json
 {
   "data": {
     "status": "ok",
     "database": "ok",
     "requestId": "..."
   }
 }
 ```
 
 Database configuration or availability errors return `503` with the standard error envelope.
 
 ## Authentication
 
 Reserved for the authentication phase; not implemented through Phase 3.
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `POST` | `/auth/register` | Create customer account; validate unique email and password policy. |
 | `POST` | `/auth/login` | Verify password, rotate session identifier, create server-side session. |
 | `POST` | `/auth/logout` | Revoke current session and expire cookie. |
 | `GET` | `/auth/me` | Return current user or `401`. |
 | `GET` | `/auth/csrf` | Issue/refresh a CSRF token bound to the current session; login/register bootstrap must be protected against login CSRF as well. |
 
 ## Homepage
 
 Each section has an independent endpoint and can be requested, failed, and refreshed separately by the frontend. Responses currently use `Cache-Control: no-store`; cache policy can be revisited for public catalog data independently of this API contract.
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/home/hero-banners` | Active banners ordered by `sort_order`. |
 | `GET` | `/home/best-sellers` | Products ranked by completed units sold in the last 30 days. |
 | `GET` | `/home/special-deals` | Active, in-window offers with available inventory and `compare_at_price_minor > price_minor`, ordered by discount percentage descending. |
 | `GET` | `/home/popular-categories` | Categories ranked by completed units sold in the last 30 days. |
 
 Each accepts optional `limit` (integer, range `1..20`; default `3` for hero banners and `8` for other sections). Each endpoint has its own response and frontend loading/error state.
 
 `GET /home/hero-banners` response:
 
 ```json
 {
   "data": [
     {
       "id": 1,
       "title": "Explore your next adventure",
       "imageUrl": "/images/hero-banner.svg",
       "targetUrl": "/store",
       "sortOrder": 1
     }
   ],
   "meta": { "limit": 3 }
 }
 ```
 
 `GET /home/best-sellers` response:
 
 ```json
 {
   "data": [
     {
       "id": 1,
       "slug": "starlight-odyssey",
       "name": "Starlight Odyssey",
       "description": "A fictional role-playing adventure.",
       "imageUrl": null,
       "unitsSold": 12,
       "lowestOffer": {
         "offerId": 1,
         "priceMinor": 1899,
         "compareAtPriceMinor": 4999,
         "currency": "EUR",
         "platform": { "code": "pc", "name": "PC" },
         "region": { "code": "global", "name": "Global" },
         "availableQuantity": 0,
         "discountPercent": 62
       }
     }
   ],
   "meta": { "limit": 8 }
 }
 ```
 
 `GET /home/special-deals` response:
 
 ```json
 {
   "data": [
     {
       "offerId": 1,
       "product": {
         "id": 1,
         "slug": "starlight-odyssey",
         "name": "Starlight Odyssey",
         "imageUrl": null
       },
       "priceMinor": 1899,
       "compareAtPriceMinor": 4999,
       "currency": "EUR",
       "platform": { "code": "pc", "name": "PC" },
       "region": { "code": "global", "name": "Global" },
       "availableQuantity": 4,
       "discountPercent": 62
     }
   ],
   "meta": { "limit": 8 }
 }
 ```
 
 `discountPercent` is calculated by the API from integer minor-unit values as a whole percentage; the client does not supply it. Only offers with inventory greater than zero qualify for this endpoint.
 
 `GET /home/popular-categories` response:
 
 ```json
 {
   "data": [
     { "id": 1, "slug": "role-playing", "name": "Role-playing", "unitsSold": 12 }
   ],
   "meta": { "limit": 8 }
 }
 ```
 
 For best sellers and popular categories, only orders with `status="paid"` and `paid_at` within the rolling 30-day period count. With no matching paid sales the endpoint returns `{"data":[],"meta":{"limit":8}}`.
 
 ## Catalog, search, product
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/products` | Product catalog with bounded filters, sorting, and pagination. |
 | `GET` | `/categories` | Active category filter options. |
 | `GET` | `/platforms` | Active platform filter options. |
 | `GET` | `/regions` | Active region filter options. |
 | `GET` | `/search` | Global search with typo and partial-word tolerance. |
 | `GET` | `/products/{slug}` | Active product details and approved sellers' active offers for comparison. |
 
 `GET /products` query parameters:
 
 - `page` (default `1`, positive integer)
 - `perPage` (default `20`, integer `1..48`)
 - `platform`, `region`, and `category` (active code/slug values)
 - `currency` (three-letter code, default `EUR`)
 - `minPriceMinor`, `maxPriceMinor` (non-negative integer minor units in the selected currency)
 - `sort`: `newest` (default), `price_asc`, `price_desc`, or `popular`
 
 The catalog lists active products. `lowestOffer` is the least expensive matching active offer in the selected currency and optional platform/region filters; it is `null` when the product has no matching active offer. An offer with no available keys is still represented with `availableQuantity: 0`. Price filters apply to the selected offer after currency/platform/region filters. Products are ordered deterministically within each sort. `popular` uses paid units from the last 30 days and breaks ties by newest product.
 
 Paginated response:
 
 ```json
 {
   "data": [
     {
       "id": 1,
       "slug": "starlight-odyssey",
       "name": "Starlight Odyssey",
       "description": "A fictional role-playing adventure.",
       "imageUrl": null,
       "lowestOffer": {
         "offerId": 1,
         "priceMinor": 1899,
         "compareAtPriceMinor": 4999,
         "currency": "EUR",
         "platform": { "code": "pc", "name": "PC" },
         "region": { "code": "global", "name": "Global" },
         "availableQuantity": 0,
         "discountPercent": 62
       }
     }
   ],
   "meta": { "page": 1, "perPage": 20, "total": 3, "sort": "newest", "currency": "EUR" }
 }
 ```
 
 Invalid, unsupported, or out-of-range query values return `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` with a `fields` map. An empty page returns `200`, an empty `data` array, and pagination metadata.
 
 Lookup endpoints accept no query parameters and return active options. Categories are ordered by `sort_order` then name; platforms and regions are ordered by name:
 
 ```json
 { "data": [{ "id": 1, "slug": "action", "name": "Action" }], "meta": { "limit": 100 } }
 { "data": [{ "id": 1, "code": "pc", "name": "PC" }], "meta": { "limit": 100 } }
 { "data": [{ "id": 1, "code": "global", "name": "Global" }], "meta": { "limit": 100 } }
 ```
 
 The three examples correspond to `/categories`, `/platforms`, and `/regions`, respectively.
 
 `compareAtPriceMinor` is null when the offer has no advertised comparison price. The API calculates any displayed discount from the compare-at and current prices, in the offer's currency; it must not trust a client-supplied percentage. An offer is eligible for the special-deals section only when the compare-at price is greater than the current price and the offer is active, in its deal window, and has available inventory.
 
 `GET /search` accepts:
 
 - `q` (required; 2–100 normalized letters/numbers; raw input up to 200 characters)
 - `page` (default `1`, positive integer up to `10000`)
 - `perPage` (default `20`, integer `1..48`)
 - The same `platform`, `region`, `category`, `currency`, `minPriceMinor`, and `maxPriceMinor` filters as `/products`
 - `sort`: `relevance` (default), `newest`, `price_asc`, `price_desc`, or `popular`
 
 Queries are Unicode NFKC-normalized, case-folded, and reduced to letter/number tokens with collapsed whitespace. MySQL FULLTEXT natural-language and token-prefix matches are ranked first. When fewer than eight FULLTEXT candidates are found, the API merges up to 1,000 candidates from the derived product-name gram index. It applies the product's catalog filters before scoring title similarity in PHP, which is limited to 100 products; ordinary catalog requests do not invoke fuzzy scoring.
 
 Search response:
 
 ```json
 {
   "data": [
     {
       "id": 1,
       "slug": "starlight-odyssey",
       "name": "Starlight Odyssey",
       "description": "A fictional role-playing adventure.",
       "imageUrl": "/images/starlight-odyssey.svg",
       "lowestOffer": {
         "offerId": 1,
         "priceMinor": 1899,
         "compareAtPriceMinor": 4999,
         "currency": "EUR",
         "platform": { "code": "pc", "name": "PC" },
         "region": { "code": "global", "name": "Global" },
         "availableQuantity": 0,
         "discountPercent": 62
       }
     }
   ],
   "meta": {
     "q": "starlight ody",
     "page": 1,
     "perPage": 20,
     "total": 1,
     "sort": "relevance",
     "currency": "EUR",
     "candidateLimit": 100,
     "capped": false
   }
 }
 ```
 
 `meta.total` describes the filtered, ranked results in the bounded scored set. `capped` is true when 100 eligible scoring candidates (or the 1,000-result lexical pool) are reached; in that case, more matches may exist beyond this page set. Invalid or too-short queries return `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`; an unmatched query returns `200` with empty `data`. Search-specific request rate limiting is deferred to Phase 6; query length, pagination, and candidate count are bounded in this phase.
 
 `GET /products/{slug}` returns `404 NOT_FOUND` when the product is missing or inactive. Only active products and active offers from approved sellers with active platform/region options are exposed. Offers include zero-stock rows so availability is explicit and are grouped by currency, then ordered by price and offer ID within each currency; amounts in different currencies are not treated as directly comparable. A product with no qualifying offers returns an empty `offers` list.

 ```json
     "product": {
       "id": 1,
 ```

 # Database Design
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - MySQL 8, InnoDB, `utf8mb4`, and UTC timestamps.
 - Use `BIGINT UNSIGNED` identifiers (or consistently adopted UUIDs) and foreign keys for relational integrity.
 - Store money as `BIGINT` integer minor units with an ISO 4217 currency code. Never use floating-point columns for prices.
 - Use `created_at` and `updated_at` where records change; use explicit statuses instead of deleting records whose history matters.
 - Store password hashes from `password_hash()` only. Never store plaintext passwords, session tokens, or plaintext digital keys.
 
 ## Tables
 
 The following is a logical schema; migrations should define exact lengths, nullability, constraints, and indexes.
 
 ### Identity
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `users` | `id`, `email` (unique), `password_hash`, `display_name`, `role`, `status`, timestamps | `role` is `customer` or a tightly controlled `admin`; `status` can disable access. |
 | `sessions` | `id`, `user_id`, `token_hash` (unique), `csrf_token_hash`, `expires_at`, `created_at`, `last_seen_at`, `revoked_at` | Store only a hash of the random cookie token. Session rows permit revocation and expiry. |
 | `seller_profiles` | `id`, `user_id` (unique), `display_name`, `status`, timestamps | A seller is a user with a seller profile; approval/status is server controlled. |
 
 ### Catalog and offers
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `products` | `id`, `slug` (unique), `name`, `description`, `image_url`, `status`, timestamps | Represents a catalog item; offers carry sale-specific platform and region details. |
 | `categories` | `id`, `slug` (unique), `name`, `status`, `sort_order` | A product may belong to multiple categories. |
 | `product_categories` | `product_id`, `category_id` | Composite primary key; many-to-many join. |
 | `platforms` | `id`, `code` (unique), `name`, `status` | Examples: PC, PlayStation, Xbox. |

 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `carts` | `id`, `user_id` (unique), timestamps | One active cart per user in the MVP. |

 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `hero_banners` | `id`, `title`, `image_url`, `target_url`, `sort_order`, `starts_at`, `ends_at`, `status` | Only active, in-window banners are returned. |
 
 Best sellers, special deals, and popular categories are computed from order/offer data in the MVP rather than duplicated into mutable homepage tables. If editorial curation or query load later warrants it, add a materialized/cache table with an explicit refresh strategy.
 
 An offer qualifies as a special deal only when it is active, within its configured deal window, has available key inventory, and has a non-null `compare_at_price_minor` greater than `price_minor`. Calculate the discount from the two integer amounts in the same currency; do not persist a separate percentage that can become stale. Treat a null comparison price (or one not greater than the selling price) as no advertised discount.

 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `product_search_grams` | `product_id`, `gram`, `weight` | Derived two/three-character gram index for typo-tolerant fallback; unique `(product_id, gram)`, index `(gram, product_id)`. Rebuild when product names or active status change. |

The repeatable seed refreshes them, and `php backend/bin/rebuild-search-index.php` rebuilds them after catalog name/status changes. Search normalization uses PHP `intl` and `mbstring`; these extensions must be enabled in the backend runtime. See `API.md` for query bounds, fallback behavior, and response metadata.
 
 ## Relationships
 
 - `users` 1—0..1 `seller_profiles`: customers may also have an approved seller profile.
 - `users` 1—many `sessions`: one user can have multiple devices/sessions; revocation is per session.
 - `products` many—many `categories` through `product_categories`.
 - `products`, `seller_profiles`, `platforms`, and `regions` each have a one—many relationship to `offers`.
 - `offers` 1—many `digital_keys`: each key is stock for one specific offer.
 - `users` 1—1 active `carts`; `carts` 1—many `cart_items`; each cart item references one offer.
 - `users` 1—many `orders`; `orders` 1—many `order_items`; each item references its original offer and stores purchase snapshots.
 - `order_items` 1—many `digital_keys` after purchase (one per purchased unit); each key row's nullable `order_item_id` foreign key can refer to only one order item, while allowing multiple keys for an item with quantity greater than one.
 - `users` and `order_items` 1—many `key_access_logs` rows provide an access audit trail.
 - `products` 1—many derived `product_search_grams` rows.
 
 ## Constraints and indexes
 
 Add indexes for:
 
 - Unique `users.email`, `products.slug`, category/platform/region codes, `sessions.token_hash`, and seller profile `user_id`.
 - `offers(product_id, status)`, `offers(platform_id, region_id, status, price_minor)`, and `offers(seller_id, status)`.
 - `digital_keys(offer_id, status, id)` for availability/locking and `digital_keys(order_item_id)` for order delivery.
 - `cart_items(cart_id, offer_id)` unique; `orders(user_id, created_at)`; `order_items(order_id)`.
 - `product_categories(category_id, product_id)` and gram lookup `(gram, product_id)`.
 - A MySQL full-text index on active-search fields where supported by the chosen query design.
 
 Use foreign-key deletion rules deliberately: restrict deletes for products/offers referenced in order history; soft-disable catalog and seller records instead. Cascading deletion is appropriate only for disposable derived data such as search grams.
 
 ## Key inventory and checkout consistency
 
 Available inventory is the count of `digital_keys` with `status='available'`, not a client-provided stock value. During checkout, lock the required available key rows (for example with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) in a transaction. Assign keys and create order records atomically. A unique assignment plus transaction rollback prevents double sale. Use a consistent lock order and bounded retries for deadlock errors.
 
 The simulated payment operation must not report success until the order and all requested keys have been committed as sold. If a future real payment provider is introduced, do not hold a database transaction open during a network call: add a reservation/expiry and payment-confirmation workflow, then fulfill idempotently after verified provider confirmation.

 declare(strict_types=1);
 
 namespace App\Repositories;
 
 use PDO;
 
 final class HomeRepository
 {
     public function __construct(private readonly PDO $pdo)
     {
     }
 
     /**
      * @return list<array{id: int, title: string, imageUrl: string, targetUrl: string, sortOrder: int}>
      */
     public function heroBanners(int $limit): array
     {
         $statement = $this->pdo->prepare(
             "SELECT id, title, image_url, target_url, sort_order
              FROM hero_banners
              WHERE status = 'active'
                AND (starts_at IS NULL OR starts_at <= UTC_TIMESTAMP(6))
                AND (ends_at IS NULL OR ends_at > UTC_TIMESTAMP(6))
              ORDER BY sort_order ASC, id ASC
              LIMIT :limit",
         );
         $statement->bindValue(':limit', $limit, PDO::PARAM_INT);
         $statement->execute();
 
         return array_map(
             static fn (array $row): array => [
                 'id' => (int) $row['id'],
                 'title' => (string) $row['title'],
                 'imageUrl' => (string) $row['image_url'],
                 'targetUrl' => (string) $row['target_url'],
                 'sortOrder' => (int) $row['sort_order'],
             ],
             $statement->fetchAll(),
         );
     }
 
     /**
      * @return list<array<string, mixed>>
      */
     public function bestSellers(int $limit): array
     {
         $statement = $this->pdo->prepare(<<<'SQL'
 WITH recent_sales AS (
     SELECT offer.product_id, SUM(item.quantity) AS units_sold
     FROM orders AS purchase
     JOIN order_items AS item ON item.order_id = purchase.id
     JOIN offers AS offer ON offer.id = item.offer_id
     WHERE purchase.status = 'paid'
       AND purchase.paid_at >= UTC_TIMESTAMP(6) - INTERVAL 30 DAY
     GROUP BY offer.product_id
 ),
 inventory AS (
     SELECT offer_id, COUNT(*) AS available_quantity
     FROM digital_keys
     WHERE status = 'available'
     GROUP BY offer_id
 ),
 ranked_offers AS (
     SELECT
         offer.id AS offer_id,
         offer.product_id,
         offer.price_minor,
         offer.compare_at_price_minor,
         offer.currency,
         platform.code AS platform_code,
         platform.name AS platform_name,
         region.code AS region_code,
         region.name AS region_name,
         COALESCE(inventory.available_quantity, 0) AS available_quantity,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
             PARTITION BY offer.product_id
             ORDER BY offer.price_minor ASC, offer.id ASC
         ) AS offer_rank
     FROM offers AS offer
     JOIN seller_profiles AS seller
       ON seller.id = offer.seller_id AND seller.status = 'approved'
     JOIN platforms AS platform
       ON platform.id = offer.platform_id AND platform.status = 'active'
     JOIN regions AS region
       ON region.id = offer.region_id AND region.status = 'active'
     LEFT JOIN inventory ON inventory.offer_id = offer.id
     WHERE offer.status = 'active'
       AND offer.currency = 'EUR'
 ),
 selected AS (
     SELECT *
     FROM ranked_offers
     WHERE offer_rank = 1
 )
 SELECT
     product.id,
     product.slug,
     product.name,
     product.description,
     product.image_url,
     selected.offer_id,
     selected.price_minor,
     selected.compare_at_price_minor,
     selected.currency,
     selected.platform_code,
     selected.platform_name,
     selected.region_code,
     selected.region_name,
     selected.available_quantity,
     recent_sales.units_sold
 FROM recent_sales
 JOIN products AS product ON product.id = recent_sales.product_id
 LEFT JOIN selected ON selected.product_id = product.id
 WHERE product.status = 'active'
 ORDER BY recent_sales.units_sold DESC, product.name ASC, product.id ASC
 LIMIT :limit
 SQL);
         $statement->bindValue(':limit', $limit, PDO::PARAM_INT);
         $statement->execute();
 
         return $statement->fetchAll();
     }
 
     /**
      * @return list<array<string, mixed>>
      */
     public function specialDeals(int $limit): array
     {
         $statement = $this->pdo->prepare(<<<'SQL'
 SELECT
     offer.id AS offer_id,
     product.id AS product_id,
     product.slug AS product_slug,
     product.name AS product_name,
     product.image_url,
     offer.price_minor,
     offer.compare_at_price_minor,
     offer.currency,
     platform.code AS platform_code,
     platform.name AS platform_name,
     region.code AS region_code,
     region.name AS region_name,
     COUNT(digital_key.id) AS available_quantity,
     FLOOR(
         (offer.compare_at_price_minor - offer.price_minor)
         * 100.0 / offer.compare_at_price_minor
     ) AS discount_percent
 FROM offers AS offer
 JOIN products AS product
   ON product.id = offer.product_id AND product.status = 'active'
 JOIN seller_profiles AS seller
   ON seller.id = offer.seller_id AND seller.status = 'approved'
 JOIN platforms AS platform
   ON platform.id = offer.platform_id AND platform.status = 'active'
 JOIN regions AS region
   ON region.id = offer.region_id AND region.status = 'active'
 JOIN digital_keys AS digital_key
   ON digital_key.offer_id = offer.id AND digital_key.status = 'available'
 WHERE offer.status = 'active'
   AND offer.compare_at_price_minor > offer.price_minor
   AND (offer.deal_starts_at IS NULL OR offer.deal_starts_at <= UTC_TIMESTAMP(6))
   AND (offer.deal_ends_at IS NULL OR offer.deal_ends_at > UTC_TIMESTAMP(6))
 GROUP BY
     offer.id,
     product.id,
     product.slug,
     product.name,
     product.image_url,
     offer.price_minor,
     offer.compare_at_price_minor,
     offer.currency,
     platform.code,
     platform.name,
     region.code,
     region.name
 ORDER BY discount_percent DESC, offer.price_minor ASC, offer.id ASC
 LIMIT :limit
 SQL);
         $statement->bindValue(':limit', $limit, PDO::PARAM_INT);
         $statement->execute();
 
         return $statement->fetchAll();
     }

     public function popularCategories(int $limit): array
     {

 SELECT
     category.id,
     category.slug,
     category.name,
     SUM(item.quantity) AS units_sold
 FROM orders AS purchase
 JOIN order_items AS item ON item.order_id = purchase.id
 JOIN offers AS offer ON offer.id = item.offer_id
 JOIN products AS product ON product.id = offer.product_id AND product.status = 'active'
 JOIN product_categories AS product_category ON product_category.product_id = product.id

 SQL);

 # REST API
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - Base path: `/api/v1`; all endpoints return JSON.
 - Browser calls use same-origin HTTPS. Authenticated endpoints (implemented in a later phase) use an `HttpOnly` session cookie.
 - Money uses `{ "amountMinor": 1299, "currency": "EUR" }`.
 - Paginated lists use `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "page": 1, "perPage": 24, "total": 42 } }`. Bounded section and lookup lists use `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "limit": 8 } }`.
 - Errors use `{ "error": { "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR", "message": "...", "fields": {} , "requestId": "..." } }`. Omit `fields` when inapplicable. Never return SQL, stack traces, secrets, or key ciphertext.
 - Use `400` for malformed input, `401` for missing/invalid authentication, `403` for insufficient permission/CSRF failure, `404` for missing resources, `409` for conflicts/insufficient inventory, `422` for semantic validation failures, and `429` for throttling.
 - Apply bounded pagination and allowlisted sort fields/directions. Never interpolate unchecked request values into SQL.
 - State-changing requests require CSRF validation. Do not enable permissive CORS.
 
 ## Implemented scope through Phase 3
 
 Phases 2B and 3 implement the health check, product catalog and reference-data lookups, four independent homepage endpoints, product search, and product detail with seller-offer comparison. Authentication, registration, login/logout, cart, checkout, orders, and digital-key delivery remain future-phase contracts.
 
 An empty result is a successful response (`200`) with `"data": []`. The API does not invent sales or inventory to populate a section. The current seed contains 30 active game products and five illustrative demo offers, but no completed orders or digital keys. Best sellers and popular categories therefore remain empty, and special deals require available digital-key inventory.
 
 The demo products span 11 categories. The five seeded offers are distributed across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S and the Global, Europe, and United States regions; all have zero key inventory. Their prices are illustrative only. Game cover image references are deferred, so seeded products currently return `imageUrl: null`.
 
 ## Health
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/health` | Verify API and database connectivity. |
 
 Successful response (`200`):
 
 ```json
 {
   "data": {
     "status": "ok",
     "database": "ok",
     "requestId": "..."
   }
 }
 ```
 
 Database configuration or availability errors return `503` with the standard error envelope.
 
 ## Authentication
 
 Reserved for the authentication phase; not implemented through Phase 3.
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `POST` | `/auth/register` | Create customer account; validate unique email and password policy. |
 | `POST` | `/auth/login` | Verify password, rotate session identifier, create server-side session. |
 | `POST` | `/auth/logout` | Revoke current session and expire cookie. |
 | `GET` | `/auth/me` | Return current user or `401`. |
 | `GET` | `/auth/csrf` | Issue/refresh a CSRF token bound to the current session; login/register bootstrap must be protected against login CSRF as well. |
 
 ## Homepage
 
 Each section has an independent endpoint and can be requested, failed, and refreshed separately by the frontend. Responses currently use `Cache-Control: no-store`; cache policy can be revisited for public catalog data independently of this API contract.
 
 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/home/hero-banners` | Active banners ordered by `sort_order`. |
 | `GET` | `/home/best-sellers` | Products ranked by completed units sold in the last 30 days. |

 | `GET` | `/home/popular-categories` | Categories ranked by completed units sold in the last 30 days. |

 ```json
 }
 ```

 | Method | Path | Purpose |
 |---|---|---|
 | `GET` | `/products` | Product catalog with bounded filters, sorting, and pagination. |

 `GET /products` query parameters:

 Lookup endpoints accept no query parameters and return active options. Categories are ordered by `sort_order` then name; platforms and regions are ordered by name:

 # Database Design
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - MySQL 8, InnoDB, `utf8mb4`, and UTC timestamps.
 - Use `BIGINT UNSIGNED` identifiers (or consistently adopted UUIDs) and foreign keys for relational integrity.
 - Store money as `BIGINT` integer minor units with an ISO 4217 currency code. Never use floating-point columns for prices.
 - Use `created_at` and `updated_at` where records change; use explicit statuses instead of deleting records whose history matters.
 - Store password hashes from `password_hash()` only. Never store plaintext passwords, session tokens, or plaintext digital keys.
 
 ## Tables
 
 The following is a logical schema; migrations should define exact lengths, nullability, constraints, and indexes.
 
 ### Identity
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `users` | `id`, `email` (unique), `password_hash`, `display_name`, `role`, `status`, timestamps | `role` is `customer` or a tightly controlled `admin`; `status` can disable access. |
 | `sessions` | `id`, `user_id`, `token_hash` (unique), `csrf_token_hash`, `expires_at`, `created_at`, `last_seen_at`, `revoked_at` | Store only a hash of the random cookie token. Session rows permit revocation and expiry. |
 | `seller_profiles` | `id`, `user_id` (unique), `display_name`, `status`, timestamps | A seller is a user with a seller profile; approval/status is server controlled. |
 
 ### Catalog and offers
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `products` | `id`, `slug` (unique), `name`, `description`, `image_url`, `status`, timestamps | Represents a catalog item; offers carry sale-specific platform and region details. |
 | `categories` | `id`, `slug` (unique), `name`, `status`, `sort_order` | A product may belong to multiple categories. |
 | `product_categories` | `product_id`, `category_id` | Composite primary key; many-to-many join. |
 | `platforms` | `id`, `code` (unique), `name`, `status` | Examples: PC, PlayStation, Xbox. |
 | `regions` | `id`, `code` (unique), `name`, `status` | Examples: global, EU, US. |
 | `offers` | `id`, `product_id`, `seller_id`, `platform_id`, `region_id`, `price_minor`, `compare_at_price_minor` (nullable), `currency`, `status`, `deal_starts_at`, `deal_ends_at`, timestamps | `seller_id` references `seller_profiles`; an offer identifies what is being sold and by whom. `price_minor` is the current selling price. `compare_at_price_minor` is the reference price used to calculate and display a discount; it is null when no comparison price is advertised. |
 | `digital_keys` | `id`, `offer_id`, `ciphertext`, `nonce`, `key_version`, `status`, `order_item_id` (nullable foreign key), timestamps | `status`: `available`, `sold`, or `disabled`. Ciphertext is authenticated-encrypted; each key row can be assigned to at most one order item. Never expose this table directly. |
 
 ### Shopping and order history
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `carts` | `id`, `user_id` (unique), timestamps | One active cart per user in the MVP. |
 | `cart_items` | `id`, `cart_id`, `offer_id`, `quantity`, timestamps | Unique `(cart_id, offer_id)`; quantity is positive and bounded by available keys at checkout. |
 | `orders` | `id`, `user_id`, `status`, `currency`, `subtotal_minor`, `total_minor`, `idempotency_key`, `created_at`, `paid_at` | Unique `(user_id, idempotency_key)` when an idempotency key is supplied. Simulated payment status is recorded here. |
 | `order_items` | `id`, `order_id`, `offer_id`, `product_name_snapshot`, `seller_name_snapshot`, `platform_name_snapshot`, `region_name_snapshot`, `quantity`, `unit_price_minor`, `currency` | Immutable purchase-time snapshots; offer may later change or be disabled. |
 | `key_access_logs` | `id`, `user_id`, `order_item_id`, `accessed_at`, `request_id` | Audit metadata only. Never store the returned plaintext key in logs. |
 
 ### Homepage content
 
 | Table | Important columns | Notes |
 |---|---|---|
 | `hero_banners` | `id`, `title`, `image_url`, `target_url`, `sort_order`, `starts_at`, `ends_at`, `status` | Only active, in-window banners are returned. |
 
 Best sellers, special deals, and popular categories are computed from order/offer data in the MVP rather than duplicated into mutable homepage tables. If editorial curation or query load later warrants it, add a materialized/cache table with an explicit refresh strategy.
 
 An offer qualifies as a special deal only when it is active, within its configured deal window, has available key inventory, and has a non-null `compare_at_price_minor` greater than `price_minor`. Calculate the discount from the two integer amounts in the same currency; do not persist a separate percentage that can become stale. Treat a null comparison price (or one not greater than the selling price) as no advertised discount.
 
 The repeatable catalog seed creates 30 active games across 11 categories and 73 active offers, with two or three offers per game. Five seller profiles provide EUR price comparisons using PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Global, Europe, and United States regions. The five existing offer rows are retained; the seed adds the remaining offers idempotently. It does not create order or digital-key rows. The frontend hides availability labels, while the API and future checkout logic continue to use actual digital-key inventory. The seed aborts rather than repurposing a legacy offer if it has keys, order items, or cart items.
 
 `products.image_url` is nullable and already supports external HTTPS references. Game cover references are deferred; products currently have no cover images. The intended source is IGDB's [cover image API](https://api-docs.igdb.com/#images), with visible attribution and rights confirmation before any commercial deployment. No IGDB credentials belong in the repository or runtime application.

 |---|---|---|
 | `product_search_grams` | `product_id`, `gram`, `weight` | Derived two/three-character gram index for typo-tolerant fallback; unique `(product_id, gram)`, index `(gram, product_id)`. Rebuild when product names or active status change. |
 
 MySQL `FULLTEXT` over product name and description provides first-pass relevance and token-prefix search. Gram rows are derived data generated from normalized active product names. The repeatable seed refreshes them, and `php backend/bin/rebuild-search-index.php` rebuilds them after catalog name/status changes. Search normalization uses PHP `intl` and `mbstring`; these extensions must be enabled in the backend runtime. See `API.md` for query bounds, fallback behavior, and response metadata.
 
 ## Relationships
 
 - `users` 1—0..1 `seller_profiles`: customers may also have an approved seller profile.
 - `users` 1—many `sessions`: one user can have multiple devices/sessions; revocation is per session.
 - `products` many—many `categories` through `product_categories`.
 - `products`, `seller_profiles`, `platforms`, and `regions` each have a one—many relationship to `offers`.
 - `offers` 1—many `digital_keys`: each key is stock for one specific offer.
 - `users` 1—1 active `carts`; `carts` 1—many `cart_items`; each cart item references one offer.
 - `users` 1—many `orders`; `orders` 1—many `order_items`; each item references its original offer and stores purchase snapshots.
 - `order_items` 1—many `digital_keys` after purchase (one per purchased unit); each key row's nullable `order_item_id` foreign key can refer to only one order item, while allowing multiple keys for an item with quantity greater than one.
 - `users` and `order_items` 1—many `key_access_logs` rows provide an access audit trail.
 - `products` 1—many derived `product_search_grams` rows.
 
 ## Constraints and indexes
 
 Add indexes for:
 
 - Unique `users.email`, `products.slug`, category/platform/region codes, `sessions.token_hash`, and seller profile `user_id`.
 - `offers(product_id, status)`, `offers(platform_id, region_id, status, price_minor)`, and `offers(seller_id, status)`.
 - `digital_keys(offer_id, status, id)` for availability/locking and `digital_keys(order_item_id)` for order delivery.
 - `cart_items(cart_id, offer_id)` unique; `orders(user_id, created_at)`; `order_items(order_id)`.
 - `product_categories(category_id, product_id)` and gram lookup `(gram, product_id)`.
 - A MySQL full-text index on active-search fields where supported by the chosen query design.
 
 Use foreign-key deletion rules deliberately: restrict deletes for products/offers referenced in order history; soft-disable catalog and seller records instead. Cascading deletion is appropriate only for disposable derived data such as search grams.
 
 ## Key inventory and checkout consistency
 
 Available inventory is the count of `digital_keys` with `status='available'`, not a client-provided stock value. During checkout, lock the required available key rows (for example with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) in a transaction. Assign keys and create order records atomically. A unique assignment plus transaction rollback prevents double sale. Use a consistent lock order and bounded retries for deadlock errors.
 
 The simulated payment operation must not report success until the order and all requested keys have been committed as sold. If a future real payment provider is introduced, do not hold a database transaction open during a network call: add a reservation/expiry and payment-confirmation workflow, then fulfill idempotently after verified provider confirmation.
